To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of three intragenically located DNA probes (p114.12, DX 13, and p482.6) in combination allows the identification of 98% of the informative females.

1) 63% of the females were informative for their carrier status, 2) the most informative probe is DX 13 (59% informative females), and 3) by using probes p114. 12, p482, and DX 12, almost 98 of all the informative women could be detected.

63% of all females are informative for their carrier status with one or more of the probes, that the most informative intragenically located probes are p482.6 and p114.12 and the most informative probe is DX 13 (a linked probe), that 98% of informative females are detected with probes p114. 12, p4826, and DX13, and that in 71% of cases prenatal diagnosis is feasible.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the detection of hemophilic carriers by DNA analysis with the use of three intragenes and one linked probe.
the development of a DNA test for hemophilia A that can be used for carrier detection and prenatal diagnosis.
the detection of hemophilic carriers by DNA analysis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in our hands, the combined use of intragenic probes p114.2 and p482.6 and of the linked probe DX 13 is a powerful method for the detection of carriers.
the use of multiple DNA probes for prenatal diagnosis of hemophilia A carrier detection is a reliable method with a high yield of informative females.
DNA analysis with multiple probes is the method of choice for the detection of carriers in families with a family diagnosis of hemophilia A.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the combination of intragenic probes p114. 12, p4826, and DX13 is a very useful approach to detect hemophilia A carriers.
the use of three intragenetic probes in combination is the most efficient way to identify the carrier state in hemophilia A.
the combined use of intragenic and linked DNA probes is a powerful tool for carrier detection in families with hemophilia A.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of multiple intragenic probes is a reliable way to identify hemophilia A carriers.
the combination of intragenic and linked probes allows for the detection of almost all hemophilia A carriers.
, for the diagnosis of hemophilia A, the use of multiple probes, especially linked probes and intragenic probes, is recommended.
